summary: Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (~1981–1987) and at Sichuan University (~1987).

Bingtao Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ma completed an MA at Peking University in 2008 and earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha studied philosophy at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, then earned an A.M. (1920) and Ph.D. (1924) at Harvard. He directed the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954) and the Bihar Tribal Research Institute (1956–1959).

Birgit Kellner works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned a doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura, held posts at Heidelberg University and the University of Vienna, and led the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (2020–2023).

Bisheshwar Nath Reu was an Indologist and historian who studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Department at Sumer Public Library (attested 1933) and headed the Government Museum Jodhpur and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.

Biswajit Biswas is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and has been affiliated with The Asiatic Society as a research scholar and fellow (attested 2026).
Biswanath Banerjee was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a position at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society.

Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He serves as a professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018) and on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.
Bo Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jiang earned a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University (~1957–1972) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander, and held a post at Uppsala University from ~1974 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).
Bokar Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1962–1989). He held a post at Bokar Monastery from approximately 1984 to 2004.

Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under the doctoral supervision of Stephen F. Teiser.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and served as a professor of philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).

Boris Turayev was a historian who studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (~1887–1891). He held academic posts at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1896–1914) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1922–1930) and worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1928–1937).

Boris Vladimirtsov worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied at St. Petersburg University and under Antoine Meillet, later holding posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1915–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).

Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Śrī Siṃha Shedra and under traditional teachers Tubten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Boyd Michailovsky is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1976–1978) and Langues et Civilisations à Tradition Orale (attested 1990).
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Byrski. She serves on the faculty at the University of Warsaw (attested 2026).
